w: Completed in 1575 and rebuilt more than once since, this Renaissance city gate still guards the old approach into Gdańsk's centre under three names at once — Polish, Kashubian, German — a small reminder of how many hands have ruled this stretch of Baltic coast. Regional heritage listed, still doing its job.
_facts: 16th-century city gate, completed 1575
Known as Brama Wyżynna (Polish), Wësokô Brôma (Kashubian), Hohes Tor (German)
Repeatedly renovated; one of the city's most important landmarks
On the regional heritage list

w: Finished in 1681 and consecrated four years later, this Baroque chapel was raised as an annex to St. Mary's Church next door and still carries its full formal mouthful of a name — dedicated to the Holy Spirit, Andrew the Apostle and John the Baptist. Mass is held here only on select occasions.
s: Baroque chapel tucked beside St Mary's
_facts: Baroque Roman Catholic church in Śródmieście, Gdańsk
Completed 1681, consecrated 1685
Also known as the Holy Spirit Church; part of St. Mary's Church, hosts Mass on certain occasions
On the regional heritage list

w: Rebuilt after wartime destruction, this eighteenth-century merchant's townhouse on Long Lane, within the Royal Route, is now a branch of Gdańsk's historical museum — and one of only a handful of surviving eighteenth-century merchant houses anywhere in Europe that visitors can actually walk through, room by room.
s: One of Europe's few walkable 18th-c merchant houses
_facts: Reconstructed 18th-century merchant house on Ulica Długa (Long Lane), within the Royal Route
Houses a museum, a branch of Muzeum Gdańska
One of only a few 18th-century merchant town houses in Europe open to visitors

n: Third Millennium John Paul II Bridge
w: Opened on 9 November 2001 to mark the turn of the millennium, this cable-stayed span throws Gdańsk's Northern Port across the sluggish "Dead Vistula" and onto the Tricity ring road — a modern landmark named for a pope, on a coastline more used to older monuments.
_facts: Cable-stayed road bridge, opened 9 November 2001
Also known as the Third Millennium Bridge
Links the Northern Port of Gdańsk with the Tricity Ring Road (S7)
Crosses the Dead Vistula (Martwa Wisła)

w: Built in 1885-87 as the largest synagogue in what was then the Free City of Danzig, the Neue Synagoge stood for barely half a century before the Free City's own authorities tore it down in May 1939 — months ahead of the war that would go on to erase much of the community it had served.
_facts: German: Neue Synagoge; synagogue of the Jewish Community of Danzig
Built 1885-1887 on Reitbahnstraße (now Bogusławski Street)
Largest synagogue in the city
Demolished by the Free City authorities in May 1939

w: Between October 1944 and March 1945, Nazi Germany ran a subcamp of the Stutthof concentration camp on this shipyard island in the Vistula delta, forcing around a hundred Jewish women into labour here. The island still belongs to Gdańsk's ship-repair industry today, its wartime use largely unmarked.
s: A shipyard island's hidden Stutthof subcamp
_facts: River island in the Vistula delta, district of Młyniska, Gdańsk
Belongs to Gdańska Stocznia Remontowa shipyard
Nazi Germany operated a Stutthof concentration camp subcamp here, Oct 1944 - Mar 1945
Around 100 Jewish women were subjected to forced labour
